selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The S. 4189 - INSULIN Act of 2026 aims to reduce the out-of-pocket price of certain insulin products for patients in group health plans and individual health insurance coverage, expedite generic and biosimilar competition, and provide grants and resources to help uninsured individuals access affordable insulin.

affected_groups.effect: Will receive coverage for selected insulin products without deductibles and with out-of-pocket costs capped at no more than $35 per 30-day supply.
affected_groups.group: Insulin Users with Commercial or Individual Health Insurance

affected_groups.effect: May benefit from state pilot programs providing affordable insulin at $35 or less per month, as well as a centralized resource center and hotline for assistance programs.
Must remove deductibles and cap cost-sharing for selected insulin products, and ensure coverage of at least one of each dosage form and delivery device of different insulin types.
affected_groups.group: Group Health Plans and Health Insurance Issuers

affected_groups.effect: May experience expedited review processes if designated as a competitive biosimilar biological product due to inadequate existing competition.

key_provisions: For plan years starting on or after January 1, 2028, group health plans and health insurance issuers must cover selected insulin products without applying a deductible.
Cost-sharing requirements for selected insulin products are capped at no more than $35 per 30-day supply, or 25 percent of the negotiated net price after January 1, 2028.
Health plans and issuers are prohibited from imposing prior authorization or medical management requirements on selected insulin products, except for safety reasons and reasonable quantity limits.
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act regarding citizen petitions to help prevent delays in generic and biosimilar applications.
Establishes a process for the Secretary to expedite the development and review of competitive biosimilar biological products when there is inadequate biosimilar competition.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to conduct a 5-year pilot program awarding grants to 10 states to provide affordable insulin (costing no more than $35 per month) to uninsured individuals.

Requires the Secretary to award a grant to an eligible entity to establish a national resource center, a 24/7 real-time hotline, and a standardized website to help uninsured individuals find affordable insulin programs.
missing_information: Exact federal appropriations amounts for the insulin cost-sharing provisions are not specified in the updated text.
Long-term federal budgetary offsets are not detailed, as a sense of Congress notes subsequent legislation should provide offsets.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The S. 4189 - INSULIN Act of 2026 aims to reduce the out-of-pocket price of certain insulin products for patients in group health plans and individual health insurance coverage, expedite generic and biosimilar competition, and provide grants and resources to help uninsured individuals access affordable insulin.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts commercial health insurance coverage, health plan benefit designs, the regulation of generic and biosimilar drug applications, and federal grant programs for uninsured individuals needing insulin. The significance score is 75 because it introduces sweeping mandates on commercial health insurance cost-sharing and broad regulatory changes for drug approvals.
